clue.text: Suggestive mood

definitions.meaning: something suggestive hints at or points to something else
in grammar, the verb mood of plain statements of fact

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hinting at something and the grammatical form used for statements, as against the subjunctive or imperative.

clue.text: Small island of some chinchillas

indicators.note: some of the word chinchillas is taken, a short run from inside it

explanation.surface: A tiny island that is home to a few chinchillas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Ireland an islet is called by this word, common in place names such as Inchcolm.

clue.text: New gear among sand, hills is working gear

indicators.note: among says one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: dunes are hills of sand

indicators.note: new means made over, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh clothes amid the sandhills turn out to be work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal for the first 'gear', and 'among' sets the result inside the sand hills; the second 'gear' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hard-wearing trousers or overalls worn for manual labour.

clue.text: Stop in Panama

definitions.meaning: a punctuation stop of two dots
Colón is a port city in Panama, at the Atlantic end of the canal

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark is a kind of stop, and the same spelling names a Panamanian city on the canal.

clue.text: Defendable, with most of team fit?

parts.note: a football or cricket team has eleven players, so most of one is ten
fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: Can a position be held when most of the side are fit?
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or maintained against attack.

clue.text: Meat cooked in ovens

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Meat being cooked in the ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the seven letters of IN OVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the meat of deer.

clue.text: State of a hut being demolished

indicators.note: a hut being knocked down leaves its letters in a heap to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: The condition of a shack that is being pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty United States, capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Delights in Keats, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible rearrangement of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Someone finds pleasure in the poetry of Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of KEATS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate someone is to take them, as in 'the idea took her fancy'.

clue.text: In this place, letter slipped into engagement-book is passed on

parts.note: in this place means here

indicators.note: slipped into says one piece is slid inside another

parts.note: a diary is a book of engagements
a letter of the alphabet, here T

explanation.surface: A letter tucked into someone's appointment book is handed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipped into' puts the letter inside the engagement book; here 'letter' stands for one particular letter, T, which is a loose convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary title or trait is one passed on from parent to child.

clue.text: English MP has one son in stress

parts.note: taken as written, a Member of Parliament
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An English politician with one son is under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' reads as worry; it is the noun for weight placed on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the special weight or importance given to something.

clue.text: A name in California for a waterway

indicators.note: in says the first pieces go inside the state's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone names a Californian waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made channel for boats.

clue.text: Rail carriage not intended for puffers

definitions.text: Rail carriage not intended for puffers

parts.words: Rail carriage not intended for puffers
parts.note: puffers suggests steam engines, but they are smokers; the carriage is one where smoking was banned

explanation.definitionFit: Trains once had compartments marked for those who did not smoke.

clue.text: Pot and tin basin broken

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: broken says the word basin is smashed and put back together differently

explanation.surface: A pot and a tin washbasin, both damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a cooking vessel; it is slang for the drug. 'broken' rearranges BASIN as NABIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for marijuana.

clue.text: Watered garden in socks, say

definitions.meaning: sprayed the garden with a garden hose
hose is an old word for stockings and socks, so someone wearing them is clad in hose

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of spraying with a hose and an adjective for wearing hose.

clue.text: Fed up with a binder that shows signs vandalism

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: cement binds bricks together

explanation.surface: Fed up with a ring binder that carries graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as weary, but 'up' is the reversal signal on 'Fed' in this down clue; 'that shows signs' is linking padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Defacing property by spoiling its surface is a form of vandalism, often aimed at signs.

clue.text: A sty is such an ugly thing

definitions.meaning: a sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye
something unsightly that spoils a view

explanation.definitionFit: Read in two words it is a sore on the eye; as one word, an unsightly object.

clue.text: Hide unguent

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hide unguent' (8): no parse gives the answer from 'Hide'; the clue looks cut short and a search did not find the full text.

clue.text: Starting to develop northern climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A northern climb is just beginning to take shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A nascent thing is just coming into being, emerging.

clue.text: Latest addresses in Cam bridge, for example?

definitions.text: Latest addresses in Cam bridge, for example?

parts.words: Latest addresses in Cam bridge, for example?
parts.note: the last speeches at the end of a play or book, with the river Cam's bridge pointing at the last letters of a word

explanation.walkthrough: 'addresses' suggests places to live; they are speeches, and the latest are the closing ones.
explanation.definitionFit: These are speeches or sections that close a play or book.

clue.text: Learns a trick for magazine

indicators.note: trick suggests the letters are played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a trick from a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' reads as a periodical; it is a store of weapons. 'trick' rearranges LEARNS A.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal, like a military magazine, is a store of arms and ammunition.

clue.text: Get nothing back on a litre of wool-dressing

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nil means nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting no return on a litre of a woolly product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NIL ON A L as a whole; 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease obtained from sheep's wool, used in ointments and dressings.

clue.text: Ready money that is right for teller?

parts.note: ready money is cash
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Is ready cash the right thing for a bank clerk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'teller' reads as one who tells; it is a bank clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier handles money in a bank or shop, as a bank teller does.

clue.text: WWII commando's language, caught tout-side

indicators.note: outside says the caught letter and the t sit round the language

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: A wartime commando's language, caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: C and T are placed round HINDI. The Chindits were British-led special forces behind Japanese lines in Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chindit was a member of Wingate's long-range penetration force in Burma in the Second World War.

clue.text: Racecourse records order

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A racecourse keeps records of the order of finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom, in Surrey, is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous English racecourse.

clue.text: Indian instrument is troubled by pitch

indicators.note: troubled says the little word is is stirred up into a different order

parts.note: tar is pitch, the black sticky substance

explanation.surface: An Indian instrument is upset by its tuning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns IS into SI; 'pitch' reads as a musical note but is tar; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument of India.

clue.text: Cock a snook in cotton fabric

indicators.note: to cock is to tilt or knock askew, so the letters are set awry

explanation.surface: Someone shows contempt while dressed in cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock a snook' is a familiar phrase for a rude gesture; 'Cock' alone rearranges A SNOOK IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nainsook is a fine, soft muslin made of cotton.

clue.text: Host was unusually jolly

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of was appear in an unusual order

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: The host was unusually cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns WAS into SWA. 'jolly' looks like an adjective; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great crowd, as can a swarm.

clue.text: Coins buried in Treasure Island

indicators.note: buried in says the letters lie concealed within the title

explanation.surface: Coins buried on the island of Stevenson's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Reis were old Portuguese and Brazilian coins of small value.

clue.text: Confused Ravel with Debussy opening

parts.note: to ravel is to tangle or knot up

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A muddled pairing of Ravel and the start of Debussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the composer, partnered with Debussy, but it is the verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangled means caught up in a muddle, as confused things are.

clue.text: A stroke touching middle peg is clever

parts.note: a cut is a stroke, as in cricket or with a blade

indicators.note: middle means the centre letter of the word peg

explanation.surface: A cricket stroke clipping the middle stump is sharp work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute mind is sharp and perceptive.

clue.text: Instructed, reportedly, in civil wrong

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: instructed means taught

explanation.surface: Someone was told about a wrong done under civil law.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the word for instructed sounds the same as the legal term; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a tort is a wrongful act giving rise to a civil claim.

clue.text: Harvey & Co took a cut of what remained to be divided

definitions.text: Harvey & Co took a cut of what remained to be divided

parts.words: Harvey & Co took a cut of what remained to be divided
parts.note: William Harvey and colleagues dissected bodies, the remains, rather than sharing out leftovers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a firm sharing out profits; William Harvey discovered the circulation of the blood by dissection.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists study bodily structure by dissecting cadavers.
